transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we lock the program, I need to hear from rights clearance and submissions staff — are there any outstanding issues with any of the competition titles, including 'After the Floodlights'? Now's the time to flag anything before the public listing goes final.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a rights issue with 'After the Floodlights.' I reviewed the executed music and archive license this morning, and there are important restrictions: the festival may hold exactly one in-person public screening — so that's fine with the planned screening — but we may NOT publish any trailer or excerpt online. The draft program currently includes an online trailer, which would violate the license. Additionally, we must use the exact credit 'Courtesy of Northline Archive.' I should note I haven't added the license summary to the programming file yet because the signed copy arrived in my separate clearance inbox, but the restrictions are confirmed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a premiere-status issue with 'After the Floodlights.' I checked the filmmaker's signed premiere declaration against the festival database today and confirmed that the film already had a public screening at the Harbor Documentary Week. This means it fails the competition's unpublished-premiere requirement. If we retain it, it must be offered as a single special screening rather than as a competition title. I haven't updated the submission record yet because the database correction queue is still open, but the premiere-status issue is confirmed.
